title: The archive keeps more than a look
technology: museum collections, reports, retained schedules and accountability records
governingQuestion: What must survive if a Fashion Week wants its claims—not only its images—to remain auditable?
status: evidence-backed production draft; recording, interviews, specialist review and owner-final approval remain open

longform.headline: The archive keeps more than a look
longform.opening: If evidence cannot survive the season, accountability collapses back into atmosphere.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: CPHFW retains schedule, framework, article and reporting surfaces while Designmuseum Danmark preserves fashion and textiles through collection-based interpretation.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: Policy evidence, show media, production records and museum objects travel under different access and reuse rules; no single archive currently joins them.

sections.heading: Next—and the limit
sections.copy: No complete public record was located for every CPHFW show’s invitations, crew credits, production data, screening evidence, media rights, product records and long-term preservation.

longform.closing: Copenhagen’s distinction is not a claim of purity. It is the decision to make participation depend on evidence—and the obligation to keep asking what that evidence cannot establish.
